clue.text: Splash out too much, though the cricket hasn't finished

definitions.meaning: to splash out is to spend lavishly, so doing it too much is to exceed one's budget
in a cricket match the overs are still pending, so play is unfinished

explanation.surface: Someone blows their budget at a cricket match that is still being played.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a whimsical reading: split the answer after its fifth letter and it describes cricket overs still pending. An over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending beyond what one has is the plain sense of splashing out excessively.

clue.text: Munitions identified by one no longer in command

indicators.note: no longer in means the numeral letter is taken out of the decree

parts.note: an ordinance is an authoritative order or decree
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Weapons identified by a retired commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One no longer in command' suggests an ex-officer; really I leaves ORDINANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is military supplies, especially artillery and ammunition.

clue.text: Frenchman upset about Toscanini's first record

indicators.note: about means the turned name goes around the conductor's initial
upset in a down clue turns the name upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the conductor's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is annoyed about the conductor Toscanini's debut recording.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data is to record it, as in a ledger.

clue.text: Short stop in house overlooking Caribbean port

indicators.note: overlooking in a down clue puts the house above the port

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
Colón is a port at the Caribbean end of the Panama Canal

explanation.surface: A brief halt at a house with a view of a Caribbean harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a British semi-detached house. 'Short stop' suggests baseball but is a punctuation mark shorter than a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicolon marks a pause shorter than a full stop, a lesser stop in punctuation.

clue.text: Fellow keeping animal of unpredictable character

indicators.note: keeping means the man's name holds the animal inside

parts.note: Eric stands for any man's name, a fellow
a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: A man looks after a pet with a temperamental nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means irregular and unpredictable in behaviour.

clue.text: Bully a soldier on horseback

definitions.meaning: to coerce or browbeat someone into doing something
a mounted infantryman, originally carrying a carbine

explanation.definitionFit: Dragoon is both a cavalryman and the verb to force by intimidation.

clue.text: Illegal broadcaster quietly absconds, making us angry

indicators.note: running off means the soft-music letter leaves the broadcaster's word

parts.note: a pirate is an unlicensed radio station broadcasting illegally
P, piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly

explanation.surface: An unlicensed radio station slipping away silently leaves us cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a direct synonym for furious or cross.

clue.text: Picturesque scene over in hilly district

indicators.note: over in a down clue means read upwards, so the run is reversed
in signals the letters sit inside the words hilly district

explanation.surface: A pretty view across a hilly region.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'hilly district' backwards, the run sits across 'district' and 'hilly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a peaceful, picturesque rural scene, as in pastoral poetry.

clue.text: A bold opera lacking a mythological hero

parts.note: a game person is a bold one, so the article plus game means a bold one

indicators.note: lacking a means the opera's title loses one of its letter a's

parts.note: Manon is an opera by Massenet

explanation.surface: A daring opera without a legendary Greek leader.
explanation.walkthrough: MANON lacking an A is MNON.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon led the Greeks in the Trojan War in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Senior cleric visiting diocese at regular intervals

indicators.note: visiting means the cleric's title goes inside the diocese name

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and diocese in Cambridgeshire
Ven., Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: An archdeacon drops in on a diocese from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenly spaced means at equal, regular intervals.

clue.text: What suitors do to steadies, say? It's a fact

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: suitors date their steady partners, i.e. they 'date 'em'

explanation.surface: A question about courting couples turns into a statement of fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date 'em', with the casual 'em for them, is what suitors do to their steadies; spoken, it gives the Latin word for a given fact.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information or given fact, the singular of data.

clue.text: Money earned exhibiting Duchamp's type of art

parts.note: the ready is slang for cash
made, as in made a living or made money

explanation.surface: Cash earned by showing a work by the artist Marcel Duchamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' is British slang for ready money, cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Duchamp pioneered art made from ordinary manufactured objects, such as his urinal titled Fountain.

clue.text: Conservative tucks into port, disposed to go without fruit

indicators.note: go without means to sit outside, so these letters wrap the rest

parts.note: apt to means inclined or disposed to

indicators.note: tucks into means the party letter goes inside the port's name

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port, is commonly called Rio

explanation.surface: A Tory politician settles into a harbour town, inclined to skip the fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go without' looks like doing without, but here means sitting outside: the word for disposed to wraps the port with the party letter inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit related to the peach.

clue.text: Painting proficiently — but this is a bore!

parts.note: an oil is a painting done in oils
well means skilfully or proficiently

explanation.surface: Someone paints skilfully, yet their work is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' seems to mean something tedious; here it is a hole drilled into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A drilled shaft for extracting petroleum is a borehole, a bore in the engineering sense.

clue.text: Cool-sounding villain first to consume composer's meal

indicators.note: sounding says the cold word is heard, giving a homophone spelt differently

parts.note: cool means chilly
a con is a convict, a criminal

indicators.note: first to points to the opening letter of the word consume

parts.note: Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A coolish crook first eats a composer's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne (1710-1778) is a favourite crossword composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli con carne is a spicy dish of minced beef and beans, a common meal.

clue.text: Mean artist involved in extremely illegal defamation

indicators.note: extremely means the first and last letters of illegal are taken
involved in means the artist sits inside the word for defamation

parts.note: libel is written defamation
RA, Royal Academician, denotes an artist

explanation.surface: A stingy painter caught up in very unlawful slander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' is not average or cruel but narrow-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberal means narrow-minded or ungenerous, i.e. mean.

clue.text: Fair development, Tartar rulers speaking this language?

indicators.note: development means the letters of fair are developed into a new order
speaking says the rulers' title is heard aloud

parts.note: khans were the rulers of Tartar (Mongol) peoples

explanation.surface: A fair grows; are Tartar rulers talking this tongue?
explanation.definitionFit: Afrikaans is a language of South Africa derived from Dutch.

clue.text: Of necessity, exercises right on behalf of worshippers

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises
for means on behalf of
CE, the Church of England, is a body of worshippers

explanation.surface: Necessarily, one exercises a right for those at church.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforce is an old adverb meaning necessarily, by force of circumstance.

clue.text: Free lemon in bag here? It's an apple

indicators.note: free signals the letters are released and rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether lemon is free in a shopping bag, then noting it is apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' rearranges LEMON IN BAG HERE into the two-word apple variety.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blenheim Orange is an old English dessert and cooking apple variety from Oxfordshire.

clue.text: Poet's son participating in key form of drama

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: participating in means the son goes inside the other letters

parts.note: legit is legitimate theatre, serious drama

explanation.surface: A poet's boy takes part in a major dramatic genre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' reads as possessive but is 'Poet is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist is a poet who writes elegies, laments for the dead.

clue.text: Person sailing round island is linen-weaver

indicators.note: round means the weaver's name goes around the island letter

parts.note: Silas Marner, George Eliot's title character, is a linen-weaver

explanation.surface: A sailor circling an island is a cloth-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman, someone who sails.

clue.text: Cool river at end of wooded valley

indicators.note: at end of puts the river letter after the valley

parts.note: the Vale of Tempe is a wooded gorge in Thessaly, Greece

explanation.surface: A chilly river flows at the end of a forested valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' is the verb, to moderate or calm.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper is to moderate or tone down, i.e. to cool a passion.

clue.text: English medic with career to take up

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
to career is to rush along, to race

explanation.surface: An English doctor with a profession to pursue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a profession but works as the verb meaning to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea or cause is to adopt it, to take it up.

clue.text: A little woman accepts it as good will

indicators.note: accepts means the girl's name takes the word it inside

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A small woman takes it kindly.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendly relations, goodwill between people.

clue.text: Ill-mannered libertine's first cut

indicators.note: first says the libertine's word goes before the rude one

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a libertine
off means rude, as in that was a bit off

explanation.surface: An ill-mannered rake makes the first cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake-off is a share or commission, often dishonest, taken as one's cut.

clue.text: Best blooming cheat

parts.note: flowers that are out are in bloom
to do someone is to cheat or swindle them

explanation.surface: An excellent bloody fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' is the verb, to defeat; 'blooming' looks like a mild British expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat or surpass them.

clue.text: After a trip crashing violently into barrier

indicators.note: after places the jumbled trip first and the other jumble next
crashing means the letters of a trip are smashed into a new order
violently means the small word into is thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: After a fall, someone crashes hard into a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is the charade's order signal: the second jumble follows the first, though 'After' opens the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A partition is a dividing wall or screen separating spaces.

clue.text: The plant a former Times proprietor mentioned?

indicators.note: mentioned signals that the surname is heard spoken

parts.note: the Astor family, notably John Jacob Astor, owned The Times from 1922 to 1966

explanation.surface: A question about which plant a past owner of the newspaper referred to.
explanation.definitionFit: Asters are daisy-like flowering garden plants such as Michaelmas daisies.

clue.text: Get better chaff

definitions.meaning: to recover strength after illness or a slump
to tease or banter, an old sense of the same verb

explanation.definitionFit: Rally means both to recover and, archaically, to mock or tease good-humouredly.

clue.text: Wading bird changes shade

parts.note: turns means changes, as leaves turn
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A wading bird alters its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnstone is a shore bird that flips stones over to find food.
